subject: Emotions
title: Gift-Giving Psychology
description: A quick, practical guide to Gift-Giving Psychology.

hook.text: The best gifts aren't the most expensive. They're the ones you didn't know you wanted until you held them.

buildup.text: Research shows surprise increases the emotional value of a gift. Expected gifts score lower on gratitude scales.

discovery.text: Givers prefer to buy what receivers ask for. But receivers prefer unexpected gifts that show deep understanding.

twist.text: The worst gift is a gift card: zero surprise, zero effort signal. It says 'I don't know you well enough.'

climax.text: Surprise gifts activate reward circuits more strongly than asked-for gifts of equal value.

punchline.text: The thought doesn't count. The surprise does.

quiz.question: What makes a gift more emotionally valued?
